children: CEO David Ricks said he is optimistic that the drugmaker's oral weight loss pill Foundayo (orforglipron) will continue to increase its market share, particularly as the treatment launches outside the U.S.
While Foundayo is now available in "four or five foreign markets, we expect many more in the next six months," he told CNBC in an interview.
He added that international markets are "a big part of the oral GLP-1 story because of capacity and the efficiency in which we can make this medicine."

The exec spoke to the network during the groundbreaking of a new $6.5B manufacturing site in Houston where the raw materials for Foundayo and other small molecule drugs will be producted. Opening is slated for 2030.

Ricks also repeated a statistic mentioned earlier this month by EVP Ilya Yuffa at a financial conference that Foundayo has captured about one in three new oral obesity pill prescriptions. The CEO added that the figure is increasing "week over week."
In Q2, Lilly reported $98M in Foundayo sales. Zepbound, Lilly's injectable GLP-1, brought in $4.9B.

Ricks also discussed Medicare coverage of weight-loss therapies, noting that about 700,000 seniors have received a GLP-1 prescription since July 1, and about 70% of that number are for a Lilly drug. Under the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program, most Medicare enrollees pay $50 for a one-month GLP-1 supply.
Foundayo could also gain an additional indication by the end of the year for type 2 diabetes. In June, Lilly released results from the ACHIEVE-3 trial showing that Foundayo
oral semaglutide in lowering A1C and improving weight loss.

title: Eli Lilly CEO Ricks sees more Foundayo growth with foreign markets
